% \newactor{var}{name}: an actor drawn as a stick figure (UML notation)
% instead of the rectangle that \newthread draws.
\newcommand{\newactor}[3][gray!30]{
  \stepcounter{instnum}
  \path (inst\thepreinst.east)+(0.2,0) node[anchor=west, minimum height=0.8cm,
    minimum width=1.6cm, fill=white] (inst\theinstnum) {#3};
  \begin{scope}[shift={(inst\theinstnum.north)}, line width=0.6pt]
    \draw (0,1.05) circle (0.15);
    \draw (0,0.9) -- (0,0.45);
    \draw (-0.28,0.75) -- (0.28,0.75);
    \draw (0,0.45) -- (-0.22,0.05);
    \draw (0,0.45) -- (0.22,0.05);
  \end{scope}
  \path (inst\theinstnum)+(0,-0.5*\unitfactor) node (#2) {};
  \stepcounter{preinst}
  \stepcounter{threadnum}
  \node[below of=inst\theinstnum,node distance=0.8cm] (thread\thethreadnum) {};
  \tikzstyle{threadcolor\thethreadnum}=[fill=#1]
  \tikzstyle{instcolor#2}=[fill=#1]
}
% \retmess{from}{label}{to}: a dashed reply arrow (used for error replies)
\newcommand{\retmess}[3]{
  \stepcounter{seqlevel}
  \path (#1)+(0,-\theseqlevel*\unitfactor-0.7*\unitfactor) node (rmess from) {}
        (#3)+(0,-\theseqlevel*\unitfactor-0.7*\unitfactor) node (rmess to) {};
  \draw[dashed,->,>=angle 60] (rmess from) -- (rmess to) node[midway, above] {#2};
}
% sdalt environment with an optional \sdelse{[guard]} divider
\gdef\sdelseguard{}
\newcommand{\sdelse}[1]{
  \stepcounter{seqlevel}
  \coordinate (sdelse) at (0,-\theseqlevel*\unitfactor-\unitfactor);
  \gdef\sdelseguard{#1}
  \stepcounter{seqlevel}
}
\newenvironment{sdalt}[1]{\begin{sdblock}{alt}{#1}}{\end{sdblock}
  \ifx\sdelseguard\empty\else
    \draw[dashed] (nw |- sdelse) -- (se |- sdelse);
    \node[anchor=north west, font=\small, xshift=3pt] at (nw |- sdelse) {\sdelseguard};
    \gdef\sdelseguard{}
  \fi}

% ============================================================
\chapter{Introduction}

ArtistConnect is a web-based platform designed to help independent artists share their creative work and build meaningful relationships with their audiences. Artists often rely on several separate services to publish media, announce events, and communicate with supporters. Fans, meanwhile, may find it difficult to discover emerging artists in their own communities.

ArtistConnect brings these activities together in one place. Artists can maintain profiles, publish multimedia posts, create events, and interact with fans. Fans can search for artists by name, style, or location, follow creators, and engage with their content. Administrators support a safe community by reviewing reports and managing accounts. The project aims to make independent creative communities easier to discover, participate in, and sustain.

% ============================================================
\chapter{Project Overview}

ArtistConnect provides a shared online environment for independent artists, fans, and platform administrators. Its core capabilities include artist discovery, multimedia publishing, event promotion, community interaction, direct messaging, and content moderation. Rather than focusing on a single medium, the platform accommodates different kinds of creative work and emphasizes connections between artists and their local audiences.

\section{Product Perspective}

ArtistConnect is intended to operate as a standalone web application accessible through a browser. The user interface provides distinct workflows for artists, fans, and administrators. The envisioned system uses an application layer to handle business rules and a database to store user accounts, artist profiles, posts, events, and relationships between users. The project also anticipates deployment through a cloud hosting service.

The current user-interface previews demonstrate representative workflows, including creating a post, searching for artists, and creating an event. These previews illustrate the intended user experience; browser-local demonstration data should not be mistaken for completed backend persistence, live notifications, or deployed production functionality.

\section{Assumptions and Dependencies}

The project assumes that users can access a modern web browser and that registered accounts will be associated with appropriate roles and permissions. Artist discovery depends on artists providing searchable profile information, such as their name, creative style, and location. Event creation depends on artists supplying sufficient event details, and publication of ticket pricing may require administrative approval.

The full system depends on the availability of backend services, persistent data storage, and hosting infrastructure. Multimedia uploads will also require suitable file validation and storage. Features involving live messaging, notifications, recommendations, or automated moderation may depend on additional services and must be distinguished from functionality demonstrated only in the interface prototype.

\chapter{Requirements Analysis}

% \begin{guidance}[Analysis before implementation]
% Finish this section and the Use Cases section \emph{before} you discuss
% any classes, code, or UI screens elsewhere in the document. Every
% planned feature must trace to at least one requirement and one use case.
% Avoid phrases like "we plan to implement \ldots" without first explaining
% \emph{why} the feature is needed from the user's perspective.
% \end{guidance}

\textbf{Customer / Stakeholder Perspective:}
Small independent artists need a platform to host their art and foster deeper connections with their fan communities. As an artist, I want a hybrid social media and art hosting site to upload my music, images, and stories, promote events, and interact directly with my supporters through messages and videos. As a fan, I want to discover new artists near me, follow their updates, attend their shows, and interact with other members of the community. As an administrator, I need tools to moderate the platform, review applications, and keep the community safe.

\textbf{Functional Requirements:}
\begin{itemize}
  \item The system must support role-based access control with distinct permissions and workflows for Fans, Artists, and Administrators.
  \item The system must allow Artists to maintain a profile, upload multimedia content (music, art images, stories, videos), and promote their events.
  \item The system must enable Fans to maintain an "about" profile and discover new artists using a proximity-based radius search.
  \item The system must provide a messaging infrastructure allowing fans to message artists and each other.
  \item The system must allow Administrators to review prospective artist applications, respond to user reports, and manage/ban accounts violating the Terms of Service (ToS).
  \item The system must allow Fans to submit appeals on their ban decisions and have an Admin other than the one who initially banned them review the appeals requests.
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Non-Functional Requirements / Environment:}
\begin{itemize}
  \item The system must be a web-based application utilizing a 3-tier architecture (frontend web server, backend application layer, and database) to handle persistence and advanced business logic.
  \item The system must be deployed to a cloud hosting service such as Google Cloud Platform (GCP), Amazon Web Services (AWS), or Microsoft Azure.
  \item The development lifecycle must incorporate a CI/CD pipeline with mandatory pull requests.
  \item Any optional AI functionalities (e.g., content moderation, recommendation engines, or AI-generated art detectors) must be designed to respect user privacy, include human oversight, and feature fallback behavior.
\end{itemize}

\chapter{User Story}

% \begin{guidance}[Requirements traceability]
% Every requirement above should be reflected in at least one user story,
% and every user story should later map to a use case. Keep IDs or
% consistent wording so a reader can trace a requirement all the way
% through to the System Sequence Diagrams.
% \end{guidance}

\begin{itemize}
  \item \textbf{[US-01]} As a \textbf{Fan}, I want to \textbf{search for artists using a proximity-based radius} so that \textbf{I can discover and attend local shows}. \textit{(Maps to UC: Search for Artist)}

  \item \textbf{[US-02]} As a \textbf{Fan}, I want to \textbf{receive artist recommendations} so that \textbf{I can easily find new creators similar to the ones I already enjoy}. \textit{(Maps to UC: Receive Recommendation)}

  \item \textbf{[US-03]} As an \textbf{Artist}, I want to \textbf{create posts with multimedia content (music, images, videos)} so that \textbf{I can share my art and stories with my fan community}. \textit{(Maps to UC: Make a Post)}

  \item \textbf{[US-04]} As a \textbf{Fan}, I want to \textbf{comment on an artist's uploaded artwork or posts} so that \textbf{I can show my support and engage with the community}. \textit{(Maps to UC: Comment on Artwork)}

  \item \textbf{[US-05]} As an \textbf{Artist}, I want to \textbf{monitor and manage the comments on my posts} so that \textbf{I can hide inappropriate content and report abusive users to admins}. \textit{(Maps to UC: Monitor Comments)}

  \item \textbf{[US-06]} As a \textbf{User (Fan or Artist)}, I want to \textbf{send direct messages to other users} so that \textbf{I can privately communicate, collaborate, or socialize}. \textit{(Maps to UC: Message Another User)}

  \item \textbf{[US-07]} As an \textbf{Artist}, I want to \textbf{create and promote upcoming events} so that \textbf{my fans know when and where to see my shows}. \textit{(Maps to UC: Create Event)}

  \item \textbf{[US-08]} As an \textbf{Artist}, I want to \textbf{edit and update my existing event information} so that \textbf{my fans have the most accurate and current details if plans change}. \textit{(Maps to UC: Update Event)}

  \item \textbf{[US-09]} As an \textbf{Administrator}, I want to \textbf{approve prospective artist verification applications} so that \textbf{I can ensure only legitimate, non-fake artists are granted the Artist role}. \textit{(Maps to UC: Approve Artist Verification Application)}

  \item \textbf{[US-10]} As an \textbf{Administrator}, I want to \textbf{review conduct reports submitted by users} so that \textbf{I can make fair moderation decisions regarding inappropriate content}. \textit{(Maps to UC: Review Report)}

  \item \textbf{[US-11]} As an \textbf{Administrator}, I want to \textbf{suspend or ban user accounts that violate the terms of service} so that \textbf{the platform remains a safe environment for artists and fans}. \textit{(Maps to UC: Suspending Artist Account)}

  \item \textbf{[US-12]} As an \textbf{Administrator}, I want to \textbf{review and process ban appeals from fans} so that \textbf{I can reverse unfair or incorrect bans made by the system or other admins}. \textit{(Maps to UC: Unban Fan)}
\end{itemize}

% ============================================================
\chapter{Key Technical Challenges}

\begin{itemize}
  \item \textbf{AI Feature Integration:} Integrating machine learning for moderation and recommendations poses performance and privacy challenges. \\
  \textbf{\textit{Approach:}} Decouple AI processing from core traffic using scalable REST APIs and implement heuristic fallbacks to ensure uptime if models fail.

  \item \textbf{3-Tier Cloud Deployment:} Managing a frontend, backend, database, and strict CI/CD pipeline requires significant DevOps overhead. \\
  \textbf{\textit{Approach:}} Establish automated testing and mandatory pull requests early, utilizing managed cloud services (GCP, AWS, or Azure) to minimize infrastructure management.
\end{itemize}

\section*{Key Risks}
\begin{itemize}
  \item \textbf{Scope Creep:} The extensive feature set (hybrid media, messaging, AI) risks exceeding the semester timeframe. \\
  \textbf{\textit{Mitigation:}} Strictly prioritize core workflows (authentication, media, messaging) over optional AI features using agile sprints.

  \item \textbf{Content Moderation:} User-generated media and messaging introduce risks of Terms of Service violations. \\
  \textbf{\textit{Mitigation:}} Implement robust user-reporting systems, Admin review workflows, and automated moderation filters.
\end{itemize}

\section*{Competition}
\begin{itemize}
  \item \textbf{SoundCloud:}
  \textit{What it does well:} Excellent audio hosting, discovery, and timestamped comments. \\
  \textit{Where it falls short:} Lacks visual art hosting, video interactions, and proximity-based local discovery.

  \item \textbf{Instagram:}
  \textit{What it does well:} Massive reach for visual art, short-form videos, and messaging. \\
  \textit{Where it falls short:} Not tailored to independent artists, lacks high-quality audio hosting, and prioritizes viral content over local community connections.
\end{itemize}

% ============================================================
\chapter{What's New?}

Existing platforms generally focus on a single medium (e.g., SoundCloud) or cater to broad audiences (e.g., Instagram). Our project introduces a \textbf{hybrid platform tailored explicitly for small, independent, multi-disciplinary artists}.

\textbf{Key Differentiators:}
\begin{itemize}
  \item \textbf{Multi-Disciplinary Hub:} Consolidates high-quality audio, visual art, and video hosting into a single profile.
  \item \textbf{Proximity-Based Discovery:} Replaces viral-chasing algorithms with a location-based search to foster real-world, local community connections.
  \item \textbf{Authenticity \& Safety Focus:} Proposes specialized AI tools—like AI-generated art detectors and privacy-respecting moderation—to maintain a secure, human-centric ecosystem dedicated to independent art.
\end{itemize}

\section{{Alejandro Garcia Jr} -- Use Cases}

\subsection{UC: Search for Artist -- Fan}

\begin{description}[leftmargin=2.2cm, style=nextline]
  \item[Primary Actor] Fan
  \item[Scope] ArtistConnect chat application
  \item[Level] User goal
  \item[Stakeholders \& Interests]
    \begin{itemize}
      \item \textbf{Fan:} wants to quickly find artists matching their interests, including artists close by.
      \item \textbf{Artist:} wants to be discoverable by relevant fans in their area.
    \end{itemize}
  \item[Preconditions]
    \begin{itemize}
      \item The Fan is authenticated with a Fan account in good standing. Artists and Admins cannot perform this use case.
    \end{itemize}
  \item[Postconditions (Success Guarantee)]
    \begin{itemize}
      \item A list of artists matching every criterion the Fan entered was displayed.
      \item If the Fan chose a distance, only artists within that distance were listed, nearest first, each with its distance.
      \item No system data was created or changed.
    \end{itemize}
  \item[Main Success Scenario]
    \begin{enumerate}
      \item The Fan selects the search feature.
      \item The system prompts the Fan for search criteria: name, genre/style, location, and an optional distance (e.g., ``within 25 km of me'').
      \item The Fan enters one or more criteria and submits the search.
      \item The system finds registered artists matching all of the given criteria.
      \item The system displays the matching artists, each showing name, genre, location, profile thumbnail, and distance when a distance was chosen.
    \end{enumerate}
  \item[Extensions]
    \begin{itemize}
      \item[*a.] The user is not signed in with an active Fan account: the system denies the search.
      \item[3a.] The Fan submits the search with no criteria entered: the system prompts the Fan to enter at least one criterion.
      \item[3b.] The Fan chooses a distance and shares their current location: the system searches around the shared location instead of the Fan's saved home location.
      \item[3c.] The Fan chooses a distance but has neither shared a location nor saved a home location: the system asks the Fan to share their location or save a home location.
      \item[4a.] No artists match the given criteria: the system displays a ``no results found'' message and suggests broadening the search (e.g., a larger distance).
    \end{itemize}
  \item[Special Requirements]
    \begin{itemize}
      \item Search results should be returned in under 2 seconds for typical query loads.
      \item Result lists longer than 20 artists are paginated.
      \item A Fan's location is used only to run the search and is never shown to other users.
    \end{itemize}
  \item[Frequency of Occurrence] High -- expected to be one of the most common Fan actions.
  \item[Notes] Viewing an artist's profile, following, messaging, or booking an artist from the results are separate use cases.
\end{description}

\subsection{UC: Review Report -- Admin}

\begin{description}[leftmargin=2.2cm, style=nextline]
  \item[Primary Actor] Admin
  \item[Scope] ArtistConnect chat application
  \item[Level] User goal
  \item[Stakeholders \& Interests]
    \begin{itemize}
      \item \textbf{Admin:} needs enough context to make a fair, auditable moderation decision.
      \item \textbf{Reporting user (Fan or Artist):} wants inappropriate content or behavior addressed.
      \item \textbf{Reported user (Fan or Artist):} has an interest in fair treatment and being informed of any action taken.
    \end{itemize}
  \item[Preconditions]
    \begin{itemize}
      \item The Admin is authenticated with administrative privileges.
      \item At least one report exists with status "Pending," filed by a Fan or an Artist against a message, profile, or event.
    \end{itemize}
  \item[Postconditions (Success Guarantee)]
    \begin{itemize}
      \item The report's status was updated to "Resolved," with the decision and acting Admin recorded.
      \item Any moderation action taken (dismiss, warn, delete content, suspend/ban account) was applied to the reported content or account.
      \item Both the reporting user and the reported user were notified of the outcome.
    \end{itemize}
  \item[Main Success Scenario]
    \begin{enumerate}
      \item The Admin opens the reports queue.
      \item The system displays pending reports, each showing the reporter, reported content or user, reason, and timestamp.
      \item The Admin selects a report to review.
      \item The system displays full report details, including the reported message, profile, or event, and the reporter's stated reason.
      \item The Admin evaluates the report and selects an action: dismiss, warn the user, delete the content, or suspend/ban the account.
      \item The system applies the selected action.
      \item The system records the resolution (Admin identity, action taken, timestamp) and sets the report status to "Resolved."
      \item The system notifies the reporting user that their report was reviewed, and notifies the reported user of any action taken against them.
    \end{enumerate}
  \item[Extensions]
    \begin{itemize}
      \item[*a.] The user is not signed in with an active Admin account: the system denies access to the reports queue.
      \item[3a.] The selected report was already resolved by another Admin: the system informs the Admin and returns to the queue.
      \item[5a.] The Admin dismisses the report as unfounded: the system records the dismissal and notifies only the reporting user.
      \item[5b.] The Admin suspends or bans the reported user's account: the account can no longer perform any Fan or Artist actions until it is restored.
      \item[5c.] The Admin chooses to delete content on a report against a user profile: the system explains that only warn, suspend, or ban apply to user reports.
      \item[6a.] The reported content was already removed (e.g., deleted by its owner): the system notes this and proceeds directly to logging the resolution.
    \end{itemize}
  \item[Special Requirements]
    \begin{itemize}
      \item The reports queue must support filtering by report type (message, profile, or event).
      \item All resolutions must be permanently logged for audit purposes.
    \end{itemize}
  \item[Frequency of Occurrence] Low to moderate -- driven by user-filed reports rather than a routine action.
\end{description}

\subsection{UC: Create Event -- Artist}

\begin{description}[leftmargin=2.2cm, style=nextline]
  \item[Primary Actor] Artist
  \item[Scope] ArtistConnect chat application
  \item[Level] User goal
  \item[Stakeholders \& Interests]
    \begin{itemize}
      \item \textbf{Artist:} wants to promote and sell tickets to an upcoming event.
      \item \textbf{Admin:} wants submitted events to be complete and valid before reviewing their pricing.
      \item \textbf{Fan:} wants accurate, trustworthy event listings.
    \end{itemize}
  \item[Preconditions]
    \begin{itemize}
      \item The Artist is authenticated with an Artist account in good standing (not suspended or banned) and has an artist profile. Fans and Admins cannot perform this use case.
    \end{itemize}
  \item[Postconditions (Success Guarantee)]
    \begin{itemize}
      \item A new event was created, linked to the Artist, with status ``Pending Approval'' (or ``Draft'' if the Artist saved it as a draft).
      \item The event appears in the Artist's list of events.
    \end{itemize}
  \item[Main Success Scenario]
    \begin{enumerate}
      \item The Artist selects ``Create Event.''
      \item The system displays the event creation form.
      \item The Artist enters the event details: title, date/time, location (physical address or virtual link), description, capacity, and one or more ticket tiers with prices.
      \item The Artist submits the event.
      \item The system validates the submitted data.
      \item The system creates the event with status ``Pending Approval.''
      \item The system confirms to the Artist that the event was submitted for review.
    \end{enumerate}
  \item[Extensions]
    \begin{itemize}
      \item[*a.] The user is not signed in with an active Artist account: the system denies the request.
      \item[4a.] The Artist saves the event as a draft instead of submitting: the system stores it with status ``Draft'' and confirms the draft was saved.
      \item[5a.] Required fields are missing, the date is not in the future, the capacity is not positive, or a price is negative: the system flags the offending fields and asks the Artist to correct them, returning to step 3.
      \item[5b.] The event is marked virtual but the location is not a valid web link: the system asks for a valid link, returning to step 3.
    \end{itemize}
  \item[Special Requirements]
    \begin{itemize}
      \item Ticket pricing must support multiple tiers (e.g., general admission, VIP).
    \end{itemize}
  \item[Frequency of Occurrence] Moderate -- expected whenever an Artist plans a new event.
  \item[Notes] An Admin reviewing and publishing the event is a separate use case (Review Event Pricing).
\end{description}

\section{Garrett DeYong -- Use Cases}

\subsection{UC: Make a Post -- Artist}

{\bfseries Use case:} Make a post

{\bfseries Actor:} Artist

{\bfseries Preconditions:}
\begin{enumerate}
	\item The artist is logged in.
	\item The artist is allowed to post.
\end{enumerate}

{\bfseries Postconditions;}
\begin{enumerate}
	\item A new post belonging to the user is saved in the database.
	\item This post can be viewed and commented on according to provided settings.
\end{enumerate}

{\bfseries Main flow:}
\begin{enumerate}
	\item The artist selects the option to create a post.
	\item The system prompts the artist to provide post content (text, files) and post permissions (whether it is public, whether it can be commented on).
	\item The artist provides this information.
	\item The system stores the post.
	\item The system adds the post to the artist's account.
\end{enumerate}

{\bfseries Extensions:}
\begin{enumerate}
	\item [4a.] No post content provided
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item [4a1.] The system determines no post content was provided.
		\item [4a2.] The system prompts the sender to provide post content.
	\end{enumerate}
\end{enumerate}

{\bfseries Special requirements:}
\begin{itemize}
	\item For public posts, the system should update the artist's profile content quickly (within 5 seconds, ideally).
\end{itemize}


\subsection{UC: Message Another User (Beginning a New Conversation)}

{\bfseries Use case:} Message another user (beginning a new conversation)

{\bfseries Actor:} User (artist or fan)

{\bfseries Preconditions:}
\begin{enumerate}
	\item The sender is logged in.
	\item The sender is allowed to send messages.
	\item The sender has accessed the recipient's page.
	\item The recipient is accepting messages (both in general and from the sender specifically).
	\item The sender and recipient do not currently have an ongoing conversation.
\end{enumerate}

{\bfseries Postconditions:}
\begin{enumerate}
	\item A new conversation thread is established.
\end{enumerate}

{\bfseries Main flow:}
\begin{enumerate}
	\item The sender selects the option on the recipients profile to begin a message.
	\item The system prompts the sender to type the message.
	\item The sender inputs the message.
	\item The system checks and validates the message.
	\item The system creates a new conversation thread with the provided message.
	\item The system enables access to this thread to the sender and the recipient.
\end{enumerate}

{\bfseries Extensions:}
\begin{enumerate}
	\item [4a.] Message empty
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item [4a1.] The system determines no message was provided.
		\item [4a2.] The system prompts the sender to type the message.
	\end{enumerate}
	\item[4b.] Message not appropriate/allowable
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item [4b1.] The system determines the message is not appropriate in some way.
		\item [4b2.] The system warns the sender of this and prompts for message modifications.
	\end{enumerate}
\end{enumerate}

{\bfseries Special requirements:}
\begin{itemize}
	\item The recipient should be notified that they have received a new message.
\end{itemize}


\subsection{UC: Monitor Comments -- Artist}

{\bfseries Use case:} Monitor comments

{\bfseries Actor:} Artist

{\bfseries Preconditions:}
\begin{enumerate}
	\item The artist is logged in.
	\item The artist has accessed the comment section of one of their posts.
\end{enumerate}

{\bfseries Postconditions:}
\begin{enumerate}
	\item A given comment has been hidden from users.
	\item Admins have been informed, if the artist so chooses.
	\item The comment's author has been blocked, if the artist so chooses.
\end{enumerate}

{\bfseries Main flow:}
\begin{enumerate}
	\item The artist selects the manage option on a comment.
	\item The system prompts the artist to select the desired action (delete/report/block user).
	\item The artist provides this information.
	\item The system hides the comment from users.
\end{enumerate}

{\bfseries Extensions:}
\begin{enumerate}
	\item [4a.] Report option selected
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item [4a1.] The system files a report after hiding the comment, to be viewed by admins.
	\end{enumerate}
	\item[4b.] Block option selected
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item [4b1.] The system makes a request to prevent the user from interacting with the artist's posts in the future.
	\end{enumerate}
\end{enumerate}

{\bfseries Special requirements:}
\begin{itemize}
	\item The system should not delete the comment from the database; it should be stored, but not visible to non-admin users.
	\item The comment should be hidden quickly (within 2 seconds, ideally).
	\item The user should be blocked (if applicable) quickly (within 2 seconds, ideally).
	\item The report (if applicable) should be sent within a few minutes.
\end{itemize}


\section{{Nicholas Nolen} -- Use Cases}

\subsection{UC: Update Event}

\begin{description}[leftmargin=2.2cm, style=nextline]
  \item[Primary Actor] Artist
  \item[Scope] Artist Home Page
  \item[Level] User goal
  \item[Stakeholders \& Interests]
    \begin{itemize}
      \item \textbf{Fan:} As a fan I want to be able to view artist's most up to date event information.
      \item \textbf{Artist:} As an artist I want to provide up to date information about my events.
    \end{itemize}
  \item[Preconditions]
    \begin{itemize}
      \item An artist has logged into the system.
      \item An artist has already created an event.

    \end{itemize}
  \item[Postconditions (Success Guarantee)]
    \begin{itemize}
      \item An event has been updated on the artist's profile.
    \end{itemize}
  \item[Main Success Scenario]
    \begin{enumerate}
      \item The artist requests to modify an existing event.
      \item The system prompts the artist to write over the event information (e.g. event type, description, date, time, relevant images/flyers).
      \item The artist updates their event's information.
      \item The system validates the input.
      \item The system prompts the artist to review their updated event details.
      \item The artist acknowledges they reviewed their details and submits the event.
      \item The event shows up on the artist's profile to everyone who views it.

    \end{enumerate}
  \item[Extensions]
    \begin{itemize}
      \item[5a. Invalid Input]
        \item The system detects invalid input.
        \item The system displays an error message and requests the artist correct the issue.
      \item[6a.] Artist fails to acknowledge
        \item The system displays an error message stating the artist must acknowledge they have reviewed the details of their submission before submitting.
        \item The artist acknowledges their review.
        \item The artist submits their event.

    \end{itemize}
  \item[Frequency of Occurrence] Mdderate -- It is expected for artists to make mistakes uploading event information.
\end{description}


\subsection{UC: Unban Fan}

\begin{description}[leftmargin=2.2cm, style=nextline]
  \item[Primary Actor] Admin
  \item[Scope] Administrative service
  \item[Level] System goal
  \item[Stakeholders \& Interests]
    \begin{itemize}
      \item \textbf{Admin:} As an admin I want to do my job and process appeals
      \item \textbf{Fan:} As a fan I want to be appealed to access the site.
    \end{itemize}
  \item[Preconditions]
    \begin{itemize}
      \item An Admin has logged into the system.
      \item A ban appeal has been made by a fan.

    \end{itemize}
  \item[Postconditions (Success Guarantee)]
    \begin{itemize}
      \item A different admin than the banning admin has reviewed the appeal.
      \item The appeal request has been processed and the fan is unbanned.

    \end{itemize}
  \item[Main Success Scenario]
    \begin{enumerate}
      \item The admin selects the option to review open appeals from bans performed by admin other than themselves.
      \item The admin selects an appeal.
      \item The admin reviews fan submitted reasoning for the appeal along with related report material along with an automated AI recommendation based on the ToS.
      \item The admin selects an option to proceed with unbanning the user.
      \item The system removes the user's ban.
      \item The system grants the user the ability to log into the website.

    \end{enumerate}
  \item[Extensions]
    \begin{itemize}
      \item[1a.]No appeals
        \item The system shows no open appeals.
        \item The admin closes the reports tab.
      \item[5a. Appeal is invalid]
        \item The admin selects an option to mark the appeal as invalid.
        \item The system logs the appeal as invalid and removes it from the open appeals list.
    \end{itemize}
  \item[Frequency of Occurrence] High -- There will likely always be fans trying to appeal bans.
\end{description}


\subsection{UC: Recieve Reccomendation}

\begin{description}[leftmargin=2.2cm, style=nextline]
  \item[Primary Actor] Fan
  \item[Scope] Fan Home Page
  \item[Level] User goal
  \item[Stakeholders \& Interests]
    \begin{itemize}
      \item \textbf{Fan:} As a fan I want to be able to find artists similar to those I like.
      \item \textbf{Artist:} As an artist I want to get my art out there to fans.
    \end{itemize}
  \item[Preconditions]
    \begin{itemize}
      \item A fan has logged into the system.
      \item A fan has previously interacted with artists on the platform.

    \end{itemize}
  \item[Postconditions (Success Guarantee)]
    \begin{itemize}
      \item A fan receives recommendations for artists they might like.
    \end{itemize}
  \item[Main Success Scenario]
    \begin{enumerate}
      \item A fan selects the option to display artists they might like.
      \item The system retrieves the artists a fan has previously interacted with (e.g. viewed profiles, liking posts, commenting on posts, etc.).
      \item The system utilizes an algorithm to determine artists similar to the fan's most interacted with artists.
      \item The system displays a list of artists to the user.

    \end{enumerate}
  \item[Extensions]
    \begin{itemize}
      \item[1a.] New Fan
      \item The fan has logged into the system for the first time and does not have interactions.
      \item The system does not show the option to display artists they might like.
    \end{itemize}
  \item[Frequency of Occurrence] High -- It is likely fans will want frequent reccomendations.
\end{description}

\section{{Gan-Orgil Gantumur} -- Use Cases}

\subsection{UC: Suspending Artist Account -- Admin}

{\bfseries Use case:} Suspending Artist Account

{\bfseries Actor:} Administrator

{\bfseries Preconditions:}
\begin{enumerate}
	\item The Administrator is logged into the system.
	\item A user account has been reported or flagged for potential terms of service (ToS) violations.
\end{enumerate}

{\bfseries Postconditions:}
\begin{enumerate}
	\item The user's account is successfully suspended.
	\item The system revokes the user's access and permissions.
\end{enumerate}

{\bfseries Main flow:}
\begin{enumerate}
	\item The Administrator requests to view reported user accounts.
	\item The system provides the pending reports and associated user activity.
	\item The Administrator determines the user's actions violate the ToS.
	\item The Administrator submits a request to suspend the user.
	\item The system updates the account status to suspended and revokes the user's permissions.
\end{enumerate}

{\bfseries Extensions:}
\begin{enumerate}
	\item [3a.] Report does not violate ToS
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item [3a1.] The Administrator determines the user's actions do not violate the ToS.
		\item [3a2.] The Administrator dismisses the report, and the system maintains the account's active status.
	\end{enumerate}
\end{enumerate}


\subsection{UC: Comment on Artwork -- Fan}

{\bfseries Use case:} Comment on Artwork

{\bfseries Actor:} Fan

{\bfseries Preconditions:}
\begin{enumerate}
	\item The Fan is logged in with "user" role permissions.
	\item An Artist has published media that allows comments.
\end{enumerate}

{\bfseries Postconditions:}
\begin{enumerate}
	\item The Fan's comment is saved and published on the Artist's post.
\end{enumerate}

{\bfseries Main flow:}
\begin{enumerate}
	\item The Fan requests to add a comment to an Artist's media.
	\item The system prompts the Fan for the comment content.
	\item The Fan provides the comment content.
	\item The system validates the comment against business rules.
	\item The system saves and publishes the comment to the Artist's page.
\end{enumerate}

{\bfseries Extensions:}
\begin{enumerate}
	\item [4a.] Content flagged by system business rules
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item [4a1.] The system determines the content violates business rules (e.g., via basic word filters or optional AI-based content moderation, if enabled).
		\item [4a2.] The system rejects the comment and notifies the Fan.
	\end{enumerate}
	\item [5a.] Inappropriate comment reported post-publication
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item [5a1.] An Artist monitors their comments and identifies a published comment as inappropriate.
		\item [5a2.] The Artist submits a report regarding the comment for Administrator review.
	\end{enumerate}
\end{enumerate}

\subsection{UC: Approve Artist Verification Application -- Admin}

{\bfseries Use case:} Approve Artist Verification Application

{\bfseries Actor:} Administrator

{\bfseries Preconditions:}
\begin{enumerate}
	\item The Administrator is logged in and authorized to manage accounts.
	\item A user has submitted an application to upgrade to the Artist role.
\end{enumerate}

{\bfseries Postconditions:}
\begin{enumerate}
	\item The user's application is resolved (approved or rejected).
	\item If approved, the user is granted the Artist role and associated permissions.
\end{enumerate}

{\bfseries Main flow:}
\begin{enumerate}
	\item The Administrator requests pending Artist verification applications.
	\item The system provides the submitted application materials.
	\item The Administrator evaluates the application to verify the applicant's identity.
	\item The Administrator approves the application.
	\item The system assigns the user the "Artist" role and updates their permissions.
\end{enumerate}

{\bfseries Extensions:}
\begin{enumerate}
	\item [3a.] Application fails verification
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item [3a1.] The Administrator determines the application is illegitimate or incomplete.
		\item [3a2.] The Administrator rejects the application.
		\item [3a3.] The system maintains the user's current role and notifies them of the rejection.
	\end{enumerate}
\end{enumerate}



% ------------------------------------------------------------
\section{William Waweru -- Use Cases}

\subsection{UC: Follow Artist -- Fan}

{\bfseries Use case:} Follow Artist

{\bfseries Actor:} Fan

{\bfseries Preconditions:}
\begin{enumerate}
    \item The Fan is logged into the system.
    \item The Artist has an active account that is visible to the Fan.
    \item The Fan is not currently following the Artist.
\end{enumerate}

{\bfseries Postconditions:}
\begin{enumerate}
    \item The Fan is recorded as a follower of the Artist.
    \item The Artist is added to the Fan's list of followed Artists.
\end{enumerate}

{\bfseries Main flow:}
\begin{enumerate}
    \item The Fan requests to follow an Artist.
    \item The system verifies that the Artist's account is active.
    \item The system verifies that the Fan is not already following the Artist.
    \item The system creates a following relationship between the Fan and the Artist.
    \item The system updates the Artist's follower information.
    \item The system confirms that the Fan is now following the Artist.
\end{enumerate}

{\bfseries Extensions:}
\begin{enumerate}
    \item[2a.] Artist account is unavailable.
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item[2a1.] The system determines that the Artist's account is suspended, banned, or otherwise unavailable.
        \item[2a2.] The system does not create the following relationship.
        \item[2a3.] The system informs the Fan that the Artist cannot currently be followed.
    \end{enumerate}

    \item[3a.] Fan already follows the Artist.
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item[3a1.] The system detects an existing following relationship.
        \item[3a2.] The system does not create a duplicate relationship.
        \item[3a3.] The existing following relationship remains unchanged.
    \end{enumerate}
\end{enumerate}


\subsection{UC: Manage Fan Profile -- Fan}

{\bfseries Use case:} Manage Fan Profile

{\bfseries Actor:} Fan

{\bfseries Preconditions:}
\begin{enumerate}
    \item The Fan is logged into the system.
    \item The Fan has an existing account and profile.
\end{enumerate}

{\bfseries Postconditions:}
\begin{enumerate}
    \item Valid profile changes are stored by the system.
    \item The updated information is associated with the Fan's profile.
    \item Profile information is displayed according to the Fan's privacy settings.
\end{enumerate}

{\bfseries Main flow:}
\begin{enumerate}
    \item The Fan requests to modify their profile.
    \item The system provides the Fan's existing profile information.
    \item The Fan provides updated profile information, such as a biography, artistic interests, supported Artists, or profile image.
    \item The Fan specifies applicable privacy preferences.
    \item The Fan submits the updated profile information.
    \item The system validates the submitted information according to profile and content rules.
    \item The system stores the valid changes.
    \item The system applies the Fan's privacy preferences to the updated information.
    \item The system confirms that the profile has been updated.
\end{enumerate}

{\bfseries Extensions:}
\begin{enumerate}
    \item[6a.] Invalid profile information.
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item[6a1.] The system identifies invalid profile information.
        \item[6a2.] The system rejects the affected changes and informs the Fan which information must be corrected.
        \item[6a3.] The Fan provides corrected information.
        \item[6a4.] The process resumes at Step 5.
    \end{enumerate}

    \item[6b.] Profile content violates platform rules.
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item[6b1.] The system determines that the submitted content violates platform content rules.
        \item[6b2.] The system rejects the prohibited content.
        \item[6b3.] The system informs the Fan that the profile cannot be updated with that content.
    \end{enumerate}

    \item[7a.] Profile update cannot be stored.
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item[7a1.] The system preserves the previously stored profile information.
        \item[7a2.] The system informs the Fan that the update was unsuccessful.
    \end{enumerate}
\end{enumerate}


\subsection{UC: Report Inappropriate Content -- Fan}

{\bfseries Use case:} Report Inappropriate Content

{\bfseries Actor:} Fan

{\bfseries Preconditions:}
\begin{enumerate}
    \item The Fan is logged into the system.
    \item The content or account being reported exists and is accessible to the Fan.
\end{enumerate}

{\bfseries Postconditions:}
\begin{enumerate}
    \item A new report is stored with a pending status.
    \item The report contains the reporting Fan, reported content or account, reason, and relevant information.
    \item The report is available for Administrator review.
\end{enumerate}

{\bfseries Main flow:}
\begin{enumerate}
    \item The Fan identifies content or user behavior that they believe violates the platform's rules.
    \item The Fan requests to report the content or account.
    \item The system identifies the content or account associated with the report.
    \item The system requests a report reason and any additional relevant information.
    \item The Fan provides a reason and submits the report.
    \item The system validates that the report contains the required information.
    \item The system creates the report and records the relevant information.
    \item The system assigns the report a pending status and makes it available for Administrator review.
    \item The system confirms to the Fan that the report has been submitted.
\end{enumerate}

{\bfseries Extensions:}
\begin{enumerate}
    \item[3a.] Reported content is no longer available.
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item[3a1.] The system determines that the reported content is no longer publicly available.
        \item[3a2.] If sufficient information about the original content remains available, the system allows the report to continue.
        \item[3a3.] Otherwise, the system informs the Fan that the report cannot be completed.
    \end{enumerate}

    \item[6a.] Report does not contain required information.
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item[6a1.] The system determines that required report information is missing.
        \item[6a2.] The system does not submit the report.
        \item[6a3.] The system requests the missing information from the Fan.
    \end{enumerate}

    \item[7a.] Duplicate report exists.
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item[7a1.] The system identifies an existing pending report from the same Fan for the same content or account.
        \item[7a2.] The system prevents creation of a duplicate report.
        \item[7a3.] The system informs the Fan that they have already reported the content or account.
    \end{enumerate}
\end{enumerate}

    {\bfseries Fan - Comment on Artwork}

    \begin{sequencediagram}
        \newactor{f}{Fan}
        \newinst[1]{c}{CommentController}
        \newinst[1]{s}{CommentService}
        \newinst[1]{r}{CommentRepository}

        \begin{call}{f}{requestAddComment(mediaId)}{c}{promptForContent}
        \end{call}

        \begin{call}{f}{submitComment(mediaId, content)}{c}{success}
            \begin{call}{c}{validateComment(content)}{s}{isValid}
            \end{call}

            \begin{call}{c}{saveAndPublish(mediaId, content)}{s}{commentSaved}
                \begin{call}{s}{save(comment)}{r}{newComment}
                \end{call}
            \end{call}
        \end{call}
    \end{sequencediagram}

	\newactor{a}{:Admin}
	\newinst[5]{c}{:ReportController}
	\newinst[4.2]{s}{:ReportService}
	\newinst[2.2]{ac}{:AccessControlService}
	\newinst[1]{u}{:UserAccountRepository}
	\newinst[2.5]{r}{:ReportRepository}
	\newinst[1.5]{n}{:NotificationService}

	\begin{call}{a}{getPendingReports(adminId, type)}{c}{reports}
		\begin{call}{c}{getPendingReports(adminId, type)}{s}{reports}
			\begin{call}{s}{requireRole(adminId, ADMIN)}{ac}{admin}
				\begin{call}{ac}{findById(adminId)}{u}{account}
				\end{call}
			\end{call}
			\begin{call}{s}{findQueue(PENDING, type)}{r}{reports}
			\end{call}
		\end{call}
	\end{call}

	\begin{call}{a}{getReport(adminId, reportId)}{c}{report}
		\begin{call}{c}{getReport(adminId, reportId)}{s}{report}
			\begin{call}{s}{requireRole(adminId, ADMIN)}{ac}{admin}
			\end{call}
			\begin{call}{s}{findById(reportId)}{r}{report}
			\end{call}
		\end{call}
	\end{call}

	\begin{call}{a}{resolveReport(adminId, reportId, request)}{c}{resolved report}
		\begin{call}{c}{resolveReport(adminId, reportId, request)}{s}{report}
			\begin{call}{s}{requireRole(adminId, ADMIN)}{ac}{admin}
			\end{call}
			\begin{call}{s}{findById(reportId)}{r}{report}
			\end{call}
			\begin{sdblock}{break}{[report already RESOLVED]}
				\retmess{c}{409 Conflict}{a}
			\end{sdblock}
			\begin{call}{s}{applyAction(report, action)}{s}{}
				\begin{sdalt}{[action = REMOVE\_CONTENT]}
					\begin{call}{s}{removeContent(report)}{s}{}
					\end{call}
					\sdelse{[action = SUSPEND\_USER or BAN\_USER]}
					\begin{call}{s}{setAccountStatus(reportedUserId, status)}{s}{}
						\begin{call}{s}{save(account)}{u}{}
						\end{call}
					\end{call}
				\end{sdalt}
			\end{call}
			\begin{call}{s}{save(report: RESOLVED, action, admin, time)}{r}{saved}
			\end{call}
			\begin{call}{s}{notify(reporterId, outcome)}{n}{}
			\end{call}
			\begin{sdblock}{opt}{[action $\neq$ DISMISS]}
				\begin{call}{s}{notify(reportedUserId, outcome)}{n}{}
				\end{call}
			\end{sdblock}
		\end{call}
	\end{call}
\end{sequencediagram}}

\chapter{Implementation Overview}

This section explains how the backend system is implemented at a high level. The ArtistConnect backend is built using a layered, three-tier architecture in Java, dividing responsibilities into distinct packages for data routing, business logic, and database persistence.

\section{Architecture}

The system architecture is strictly organized into major layers, each with a single, well-defined responsibility. This separation of concerns ensures that the application is scalable, testable, and easier to maintain.

\begin{itemize}
  \item \textbf{Controller Layer (\texttt{controller/}):} This layer serves as the entry point for the REST API. It handles incoming HTTP requests, extracts parameters and payloads (such as JSON data), delegates processing to the appropriate services, and returns formatted HTTP responses. It includes domain-specific controllers (e.g., \texttt{ArtistController}, \texttt{EventController}, \texttt{ReportController}) and utility classes like \texttt{CurrentUser} for session and identity management.
  
  \item \textbf{Service Layer (\texttt{service/}):} The service layer acts as the "brain" of the application, containing all core business logic and workflows. It enforces business rules, verifies permissions, and coordinates data flow between multiple repositories. For example, \texttt{EventService} handles the logic of drafting or publishing an event, while \texttt{AccessControlService} strictly enforces role-based permissions before any action occurs.
  
  \item \textbf{Repository Layer (\texttt{repository/}):} This data access layer handles all database persistence. It isolates the rest of the application from the underlying database technologies (e.g., SQL queries). By utilizing interfaces (like \texttt{EventRepository} or \texttt{UserAccountRepository}), it provides clean methods for creating, reading, updating, and deleting domain entities.
  
  \item \textbf{Domain Model (\texttt{model/}):} This package defines the core entities of the application that map to database tables (e.g., \texttt{UserAccount}, \texttt{Event}, \texttt{Post}, \texttt{Report}). It also contains critical enumerations (\texttt{Role}, \texttt{AccountStatus}, \texttt{ReportStatus}) that govern application state.
  
  \item \textbf{Data Transfer Object Layer (\texttt{dto/}):} This layer contains strictly typed objects used to pass data between the client and server (e.g., \texttt{CreateEventRequest}, \texttt{ArtistSearchCriteria}). They act as the public API contract, completely decoupled from the internal database models.
\end{itemize}

\section{Key Design Decisions}

During the implementation of Iteration II, several important structural choices were made to support the specific functional and non-functional requirements of the ArtistConnect platform:

\begin{itemize}
  \item \textbf{Centralized Access Control:} Rather than checking permissions ad-hoc inside every controller, we implemented a dedicated \texttt{AccessControlService}. Because ArtistConnect relies heavily on strict Role-Based Access Control (Admins, Artists, Fans) and account states (Suspended, Banned, Active), funneling all authorization checks through a single service prevents security oversights and reduces code duplication.

  \item \textbf{Separation of Models and DTOs:} We intentionally decoupled our database entities (\texttt{model/}) from our API payloads (\texttt{dto/}). Using classes like \texttt{CreateEventRequest} instead of accepting a raw \texttt{Event} object prevents over-posting attacks, hides sensitive internal attributes (like database IDs or password hashes) from the frontend, and allows us to validate incoming data safely before mapping it to a persistent entity.

  \item \textbf{Domain-Driven Service Segregation:} Instead of a monolithic \texttt{UserService} handling everything, the logic is highly segregated into bounded contexts (e.g., \texttt{FanCommunityService}, \texttt{ModerationService}, \texttt{ConversationService}, \texttt{PostService}). This adheres to the Single Responsibility Principle (SRP) and ensures that, for instance, the complex logic for messaging and notifications does not bloat the core artist discovery logic.

  \item \textbf{Dedicated Moderation Subsystem:} Content safety was identified as a key risk in Iteration I. In response, we designed a dedicated moderation ecosystem (\texttt{Report}, \texttt{ReportEvidence}, \texttt{ReportController}, \texttt{ModerationService}). By isolating moderation into its own pipeline, we can more easily integrate future AI-based moderation tools and provide Administrators with clean, auditable queues of user conduct reports.
\end{itemize}

\chapter{Operation Contracts}

% \begin{guidance}[One contract per key system operation]
% An operation contract documents \emph{what} a system operation
% guarantees, not \emph{how} it is implemented. Postconditions describe
% instances created/deleted, associations formed/broken, and attributes
% changed -- written in the past tense, as if describing what has already
% happened. Write one contract per team member's use cases (typically the
% one system operation in the main success scenario that changes state).
% \end{guidance}

\section*{Operation: searchArtists(fanId: Long, criteria: ArtistSearchCriteria): List\textlangle ArtistSearchResult\textrangle}
\begin{description}[leftmargin=2.8cm, style=nextline]
  \item[Cross Reference] UC: Search for Artist -- Fan
  \item[Preconditions]
    \begin{itemize}
      \item A UserAccount instance identified by \texttt{fanId} exists with \texttt{role} = FAN and \texttt{status} = ACTIVE.
    \end{itemize}
  \item[Postconditions]
    \begin{itemize}
      \item A collection of Artist instances matching every given criterion (name, genre, location) was retrieved.
      \item If \texttt{criteria.radiusKm} was given, only Artist instances within that distance of the search origin (the given coordinates, or else the Fan's saved \texttt{latitude}/\texttt{longitude}) were retrieved, ordered by distance.
      \item No instances were created, deleted, or modified (read-only operation).
    \end{itemize}
\end{description}

\section*{Operation: resolveReport(adminId: Long, reportId: Long, request: ResolveReportRequest): Report}
\begin{description}[leftmargin=2.8cm, style=nextline]
  \item[Cross Reference] UC: Review Report -- Admin
  \item[Preconditions]
    \begin{itemize}
      \item A UserAccount instance identified by \texttt{adminId} exists with \texttt{role} = ADMIN and \texttt{status} = ACTIVE.
      \item A Report instance identified by \texttt{reportId} exists with \texttt{status} = PENDING.
    \end{itemize}
  \item[Postconditions]
    \begin{itemize}
      \item The Report instance's \texttt{status} was changed to RESOLVED, and its \texttt{action}, \texttt{resolvedBy} (the Admin), \texttt{resolvedAt}, and \texttt{resolutionNotes} were set.
      \item If \texttt{action} = REMOVE\_CONTENT, the reported Post's \texttt{hidden} was set to true, or the reported Event's \texttt{status} was changed to REMOVED.
      \item If \texttt{action} = SUSPEND\_USER or BAN\_USER, the reported UserAccount's \texttt{status} was changed to SUSPENDED or BANNED respectively.
      \item A new Notification instance was created for the reporting user.
      \item If \texttt{action} $\neq$ DISMISS, a new Notification instance was created for the reported user.
    \end{itemize}
\end{description}

\section*{Operation: createEvent(userId: Long, request: CreateEventRequest): Event}
\begin{description}[leftmargin=2.8cm, style=nextline]
  \item[Cross Reference] UC: Create Event -- Artist
  \item[Preconditions]
    \begin{itemize}
      \item A UserAccount instance identified by \texttt{userId} exists with \texttt{role} = ARTIST, \texttt{status} = ACTIVE, and a linked Artist profile.
    \end{itemize}
  \item[Postconditions]
    \begin{itemize}
      \item A new Event instance was created with \texttt{title}, \texttt{description}, \texttt{startsAt}, \texttt{location}, \texttt{virtual}, and \texttt{capacity} set from \texttt{request}.
      \item One TicketTier instance was created for each tier in \texttt{request} and associated with the new Event.
      \item The new Event was associated with the Artist profile of the requesting account.
      \item The new Event's \texttt{status} was set to DRAFT if \texttt{request.saveAsDraft} is true, otherwise to PENDING\_APPROVAL.
    \end{itemize}
\end{description}

\chapter{Testing}
\section{JUnit Testing Summary}
This section documents testing of each member's implemented use cases.

JUnit integration tests use Spring Boot, MockMvc, and the H2 database to exercise the controller, service, repository, and existing administrator-report integration. The tests check HTTP responses and stored records, rather than relying only on interface messages. Mockito simulates a repository write failure to verify transaction rollback. Concurrent requests verify duplicate protection.

Coverage includes valid workflows, role authorization, artist availability, independent fan accounts, privacy filtering, text and image validation, stale edits, storage failures, required report fields, duplicate pending reports, and evidence retained after content deletion. Browser checks additionally verified saved follows after reload, account switching, profile editing and privacy, reporting and administrator resolution, and mobile layout.

\subsection*{Follow Artist -- Fan}
\williamtestcase
{WW-FA-01}
{Follow an active artist and retrieve the relationship; then unfollow.}
{Active fan account 1; active artist 1 (Luna Park). Send PUT to the follow endpoint, GET the following list and own profile, then DELETE the follow.}
{PUT returns HTTP 200 with following=true and followerCount=1. Both lists contain artist 1. DELETE returns 204; the next follow-state read reports followerCount=0.}
{Observed HTTP 200 and one follower; Luna Park appeared in both lists. Unfollow returned 204 and the count became 0.}
{Passed}
\williamtestcase
{WW-FA-02}
{Repeated and concurrent follow requests must not create duplicate relationships.}
{Send the same follow request twice for fan 1 / artist 1. In a separate test, send four simultaneous PUT requests for fan 5 / artist 6.}
{All requests return HTTP 200. Each fan/artist pair has exactly one follow row and one FOLLOW interaction. Repeated requests do not increase the follower count for the same fan.}
{Both repeated requests and all four concurrent requests returned 200. Database assertions found one relationship and one FOLLOW interaction per tested pair.}
{Passed}
\clearpage
\noindent\textbf{Follow Artist -- Fan (continued)}\par
\williamtestcase
{WW-FA-03}
{Reject a suspended artist, a banned artist account, and an unknown artist.}
{Fan 1 attempts to follow artist 1 with its suspension flag set; retries after clearing that flag and banning the linked artist account; also requests artist 9999.}
{Suspended and banned cases each return HTTP 409. The unknown artist returns 404. No follow relationship is stored for any rejected request.}
{Observed 409 for each unavailable-artist case and 404 for artist 9999. Follow repository count remained zero.}
{Passed}
\williamtestcase
{WW-FA-04}
{Enforce fan authorization and keep different fans' following lists independent.}
{Follow artist 1 with no acting-account header and then artist account 2. Separately, fan 1 follows artist 1; inspect fan 5's list before fan 5 follows the same artist.}
{Unauthenticated request returns HTTP 401; artist-role request returns 403. Fan 5 initially sees an empty list. After both fans follow, the shared artist count is exactly 2.}
{Observed 401 and 403. Fan 5's list was initially empty; its own follow returned followerCount=2 without duplicating either fan's relationship.}
{Passed}
\clearpage
\subsection*{Manage Fan Profile -- Fan}
\williamtestcase
{WW-MFP-01}
{Save valid profile text and a valid uploaded profile image.}
{Fan 1 saves display name New Fan Name, biography Love independent art, interests Jazz and art, and valid privacy values. A separate request uploads a generated 2-by-2-pixel PNG as a data URL.}
{Each valid update returns HTTP 200. Subsequent profile reads return the saved text and exactly the uploaded PNG data URL. Publicly enabled interests and image are visible to fan 5.}
{Observed 200 for valid updates. Saved text and image matched the submitted values; fan 5 retrieved the enabled public fields.}
{Passed}
\williamtestcase
{WW-MFP-02}
{Apply field-level and whole-profile privacy on the server.}
{Fan 1 saves a public profile with showInterests=false and showFollowing=false. Fan 5 requests that profile. Fan 1 then sets publicProfile=false; repeat reads as fan 5 and as the owner.}
{For the public profile, fan 5 receives HTTP 200 without interests or supportedArtists values. Once private, fan 5 receives 404 while the owner still receives 200 with their full profile.}
{Public response omitted the hidden fields. After the privacy change, the other fan received 404 and the owner retained 200 access.}
{Passed}
\clearpage
\noindent\textbf{Manage Fan Profile -- Fan (continued)}\par
\williamtestcase
{WW-MFP-03}
{Reject invalid content, malformed images, and stale edits without replacing valid data.}
{After saving Saved Name / Saved bio, submit a blank name and then a biography containing script markup. Separately submit a malformed PNG data URL and a profile update carrying an outdated version.}
{Blank-name, prohibited-content, and malformed-image requests return HTTP 400. The blank-name response identifies displayName. A stale version returns 409. Rejected requests preserve the previous stored profile.}
{Observed 400 with a displayName field error, 400 for script markup and malformed PNG data, and 409 for the stale edit. Stored Saved Name / Saved bio remained unchanged after the invalid text requests.}
{Passed}
\williamtestcase
{WW-MFP-04}
{Preserve both profile and account data when a database write fails.}
{Save Persisted Name / Persisted biography for fan 1. Configure the profile repository spy to throw a database write exception, then attempt to save Must roll back / Must not persist.}
{The update returns HTTP 503. The transaction rolls back: the profile biography remains Persisted biography and the account display name remains Persisted Name.}
{Observed HTTP 503. Follow-up database reads confirmed the previous biography and account display name; neither attempted replacement was committed.}
{Passed}
\clearpage
\subsection*{Report Inappropriate Content -- Fan}
\williamtestcase
{WW-RIC-01}
{Submit a valid report and make it available to the existing administrator queue.}
{Fan 1 reports published EVENT 2 with reason Spam and details Please review this context. Admin account 3 retrieves the pending report queue.}
{Submission returns HTTP 201 with status=PENDING and reportedUserId=2. The saved snapshot includes Austin Acoustic Night. The seeded three-report admin queue increases to four.}
{Observed 201, PENDING, owner account 2, and the expected event snapshot. The admin queue contained four reports, including the new submission.}
{Passed}
\williamtestcase
{WW-RIC-02}
{Reject missing reasons, unavailable content, and callers without the fan role.}
{Submit a whitespace-only reason for EVENT 2; report nonexistent POST 9999; report unpublished EVENT 3; and attempt reporting as artist account 2.}
{Missing reason returns HTTP 400. Missing post and unpublished event each return 404. The artist-role request returns 403. No rejected request adds a report; the seeded count stays at 3.}
{Observed 400, 404, 404, and 403 respectively. Database report count remained three.}
{Passed}
\clearpage
\noindent\textbf{Report Inappropriate Content -- Fan (continued)}\par
\williamtestcase
{WW-RIC-03}
{Prevent duplicate pending reports, including simultaneous submissions.}
{Fan 1 submits EVENT 2 twice. In a separate test, fan 5 sends four simultaneous reports for EVENT 2 with reason Spam.}
{The first sequential request returns HTTP 201 and the duplicate returns 409. The concurrent set produces exactly one 201 and three 409 responses, leaving only one new pending report for that fan/target.}
{Observed 201 then 409 for the sequential pair. Concurrent results were exactly 201, 409, 409, 409; duplicate pending reports were not created.}
{Passed}
\williamtestcase
{WW-RIC-04}
{Allow reporting deleted content only with evidence captured for the same fan and target.}
{Fan 5 captures server evidence for POST 1000; delete that post. Submit without evidence, try the captured ID as fan 1 against EVENT 2, then submit as fan 5 for POST 1000 using the matching evidence.}
{Without evidence the deleted-post request returns HTTP 404. Evidence with the wrong fan/target returns 404. Matching retained evidence returns 201 and preserves the snapshot text New single out Friday.}
{Observed 404 for missing evidence and mismatched ownership/target. Matching evidence returned 201; the saved report retained the original post text.}
{Passed}

\chapter{Setup / Installation Guide}
This guide explains how to reproduce ArtistConnect on a local computer, start both application tiers, and run the automated checks. The commands use Windows PowerShell unless a macOS/Linux alternative is given. The backend uses Spring Boot and an embedded H2 database; the frontend uses Next.js.

\section{Required Tools}
Install the following tools before starting:
\begin{center}
\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.2}
\begin{tabular}{|>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.24\textwidth}|>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.68\textwidth}|}
\hline
\textbf{Tool} & \textbf{Requirement} \\ \hline
Git & Required to clone the repository and select the project branch. \\ \hline
Java Development Kit & JDK 21, including the Java compiler (\texttt{javac}). A Java runtime alone is insufficient. \\ \hline
Node.js and npm & An LTS version of Node.js meeting the frontend's minimum of 20.9.0, with npm installed. \\ \hline
Web browser & Required to open the application. Automated browser tests additionally require Playwright and Chromium. \\ \hline
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

Maven does not require a separate installation: the repository includes a Maven wrapper. A separate database server is also unnecessary because the backend creates H2 and loads its sample records automatically. Internet access is required for initial dependency downloads. The current backend uses Spring Boot \texttt{4.1.2-SNAPSHOT}, with its snapshot repository configured in the Maven build.

Installation sources are \href{https://git-scm.com/install/}{Git}, \href{https://adoptium.net/temurin/releases/?version=21}{Eclipse Temurin JDK 21}, and \href{https://nodejs.org/en/download}{Node.js}.

\section{Environment Configuration}
Set \texttt{JAVA\_HOME} to the JDK installation directory, not its \texttt{bin} subdirectory. Add the JDK's \texttt{bin} directory to \texttt{PATH}.

On Windows, use the installer's environment-variable options when available. Otherwise, open \textbf{Edit the system environment variables}, select \textbf{Environment Variables}, create or update \texttt{JAVA\_HOME}, and add \texttt{\%JAVA\_HOME\%\textbackslash bin} to \texttt{Path}. On macOS/Linux, configure the equivalent variables through the JDK installation or shell environment. Open a new terminal after making changes.

Verify the tools before continuing:
\begin{samepage}
\begin{verbatim}
git --version
java -version
javac -version
node --version
npm --version
\end{verbatim}
\end{samepage}
Both Java commands should report version 21. Node.js must be at least 20.9.0. If a command is not recognized, correct its installation or environment configuration before proceeding.

No environment file is needed for the default local setup. The frontend expects the backend at \texttt{http://localhost:8080}. If a different address is necessary, create \texttt{frontend/.env.local}, set \texttt{NEXT\_PUBLIC\_API\_URL} to that address, and restart the frontend. A production frontend build must be rebuilt after changing this value. The backend currently permits the frontend origin \texttt{http://localhost:3000}; changing that origin also requires updating its CORS configuration.

\section{Download the Project}
Open a terminal in the directory where the project should be stored:
\begin{samepage}
\begin{verbatim}
git clone https://github.com/AGarciaJr/CSI5324-IndieDevs.git
cd CSI5324-IndieDevs
git switch william
git branch --show-current
\end{verbatim}
\end{samepage}
The final command should print \texttt{william}. If the repository is already available locally, use that checkout and confirm the intended branch instead of cloning again.

The \texttt{backend} directory contains the Spring Boot application, Maven wrapper, and JUnit tests. The \texttt{frontend} directory contains the Next.js application and browser-test scripts. Run Maven commands inside \texttt{backend} and npm commands inside \texttt{frontend}.

\section{Start the Backend}
Open \textbf{Terminal 1} in the repository root. On Windows PowerShell, run:
\begin{samepage}
\begin{verbatim}
cd backend
.\mvnw.cmd spring-boot:run
\end{verbatim}
\end{samepage}
On macOS/Linux, use:
\begin{samepage}
\begin{verbatim}
cd backend
./mvnw spring-boot:run
\end{verbatim}
\end{samepage}
The first run may take several minutes while Maven downloads its dependencies. Wait until the log reports that Tomcat started on port 8080 and that \texttt{BackendApplication} started. Leave this terminal running.

Verify startup by opening \url{http://localhost:8080/api/artists}. A JSON list of sample artists should appear. The backend root URL is not the application's frontend page.

The default database requires no manual schema creation. For optional inspection, open \url{http://localhost:8080/h2-console}, use JDBC URL \texttt{jdbc:h2:mem:testdb}, driver \texttt{org.h2.Driver}, user name \texttt{sa}, and a blank password.

\section{Install and Start the Frontend}
Open \textbf{Terminal 2} in the repository root:
\begin{samepage}
\begin{verbatim}
cd frontend
npm ci
npm run dev
\end{verbatim}
\end{samepage}
The \texttt{npm ci} command installs the versions recorded in the frontend lockfile. Wait for Next.js to report that it is ready, then open \url{http://localhost:3000}. Keep both terminals running: the frontend uses port 3000 and communicates with the backend on port 8080. The initial fan view should show the artist-discovery search controls, with the demo-account switcher beneath the logo.

Use \texttt{localhost:3000} for this setup so that the browser origin matches the backend's CORS configuration. Press \textbf{Ctrl+C} in a server's terminal to stop it.

To run the frontend as a production build instead, stop its development server and execute these commands from \texttt{frontend}, while keeping the backend running:
\begin{samepage}
\begin{verbatim}
npm run build
npm run start
\end{verbatim}
\end{samepage}
A successful build is required before \texttt{npm run start}. The browser address remains \url{http://localhost:3000}.

\section{Run the Automated Checks}
\subsection{Backend JUnit Tests}
The backend tests start their own Spring Boot test context and H2 database; the application servers do not need to be running. From the repository root, use Windows PowerShell:
\begin{samepage}
\begin{verbatim}
cd backend
.\mvnw.cmd test
\end{verbatim}
\end{samepage}
On macOS/Linux, replace the second command with \texttt{./mvnw test}. A successful run ends with \textbf{BUILD SUCCESS} and zero test failures or errors. Detailed reports are written to \path{backend/target/surefire-reports/}.

To run only the fan-community tests, execute the following from \texttt{backend}:
\begin{samepage}
\begin{verbatim}
.\mvnw.cmd "-Dtest=FanCommunityTest" test
\end{verbatim}
\end{samepage}
On macOS/Linux, use \texttt{./mvnw} instead of \texttt{.\textbackslash mvnw.cmd}.

\subsection{Frontend Checks}
From the repository root, open another terminal and run:
\begin{samepage}
\begin{verbatim}
cd frontend
npm run lint
npx tsc --noEmit
npm run build
\end{verbatim}
\end{samepage}
These commands check lint rules, TypeScript types, and the production build. There is currently no separate \texttt{npm test} script. Two existing hook-dependency lint warnings and the Next.js multiple-lockfile warning should be distinguished from errors.

\subsection{Browser Integration Tests}
Keep the backend and frontend running at their default addresses. In a third terminal, from the repository root, install the optional test tools:
\begin{samepage}
\begin{verbatim}
cd frontend
npm install --no-save --package-lock=false playwright
npx playwright install chromium
\end{verbatim}
\end{samepage}
This local installation does not change the package manifest or lockfile. A subsequent \texttt{npm ci} removes the extra Playwright package, so reinstall it when necessary. If Linux reports missing browser libraries, use \texttt{npx playwright install --with-deps chromium}; installation of system libraries may require administrator privileges.

Restart the backend and wait for startup to complete before each script so that the expected sample records are available. From \texttt{frontend}, run:
\begin{samepage}
\begin{verbatim}
node tests/presentation-regression.cjs
\end{verbatim}
\end{samepage}
This checks original demo accounts, search, navigation, existing team screens, and the added fan/admin tabs on desktop and mobile. It does not modify backend records.

After another backend restart, run:
\begin{samepage}
\begin{verbatim}
node tests/fan-community-smoke.cjs
\end{verbatim}
\end{samepage}
This checks live follow persistence, account isolation, profile validation/privacy, reporting, duplicate protection, administrator resolution, and mobile layout. It changes local demo profile, follow, and report data. Restart the backend again when the original samples are needed for a presentation.

Both scripts print a \textbf{PASS} message on success and return a nonzero exit code on failure. Screenshots are saved in \texttt{frontend/test-results/}.

\section{Troubleshooting and Resetting Sample Data}
\begin{description}[style=nextline,leftmargin=0pt]
\item[Java or Maven cannot find the JDK.]
Verify \texttt{JAVA\_HOME}, \texttt{PATH}, \texttt{java -version}, and \texttt{javac -version}. An unsupported-release error usually means that an older JDK is active.
\item[PowerShell blocks npm or npx scripts.]
Use \texttt{npm.cmd} or \texttt{npx.cmd}, for example \texttt{npm.cmd ci} and \texttt{npm.cmd run dev}.
\item[The Maven wrapper reports permission denied on macOS/Linux.]
From \texttt{backend}, run \texttt{chmod +x mvnw} and retry the wrapper command.
\item[Dependencies cannot be downloaded.]
Check the internet connection and proxy settings. Maven needs Maven Central and the configured Spring snapshot repository; npm and Playwright also need access to their download services.
\item[Port 8080 or 3000 is already occupied.]
Stop the previous server with Ctrl+C in its terminal, or close the application using that port. Retain the default ports for this guide and the browser tests.
\item[The interface opens but live features fail.]
Confirm that the backend remains running and that its artist-list endpoint returns JSON. Open the frontend through \texttt{http://localhost:3000}, not a different host name or port.
\item[Playwright cannot find its module or browser.]
Repeat the optional Playwright installation. Then, from \texttt{frontend}, run:
\begin{samepage}
\begin{verbatim}
npx playwright install chromium
\end{verbatim}
\end{samepage}
\item[Demo data reset or browser tests fail.]
The default H2 database is in memory with schema recreation enabled. Restarting the backend, including a DevTools restart, restores its seeded records. Browser reloads alone do not reset it. Restart the backend before a presentation or seed-dependent test. Some existing demo features store data in browser local storage; restarting the backend does not clear that separate browser data.
\end{description}
